question: Does the held-out construction/direction hierarchy predict raw task-functional response magnitude as well as direction, or was the normalized-Q result only angular?
evidence_status: CPU-only upper-bound screen for the preregistered H/R state program; no causal or adoption claim.

searched: v20 task-functional tensor analyses and crossfits
prior_art_and_novelty.known_result: Cell and additive prototypes predict normalized held-out Q directions at cosine .9754/.9584, but normalization discards amplitude.
prior_art_and_novelty.novelty: Fit raw cell and additive Q states on reporter-disjoint rows and predict held-out vectors without row normalization or amplitude calibration. This is the attainable upper bound for independently averaged H/R state programs.

method.folds: groups modulo 4 in {0,1} fit and {2,3} test, then reverse; balanced over direction
method.cell_program: Raw arithmetic mean Q for each fit panel-by-direction cell predicts every held-out row in that cell.
method.additive_program: Raw panel_mean + direction_mean - grand_mean predicts held-out rows.
method.metrics: For pooled and per-cell concatenated factor vectors report cosine, signed recovery dot(pred,actual)/||actual||^2, relative residual, and row-level positive-dot fraction.

predictions.pred_a_authority_raw_formula_balanced_fo: All hashes, 4x16x4608 shape, folds, formulas, finiteness, and operation counts match.
predictions.pred_b_raw_cell_states_predict_heldout_q: Pooled cell cosine >=0.85, pooled signed recovery in [0.50,1.50], pooled relative residual <=0.75, every cell cosine >=0.75, and all 48 row dots are positive.
predictions.pred_c_raw_additive_hierarchy_is_nearly_: Additive pooled cosine >=0.80, relative residual <=0.85, and it trails cell by at most 0.08 cosine and 0.15 relative residual.
predictions.pred_d_scope_is_upper_bound_screen_only: No model/GPU call, H/R or v21 outcome, fit to held-out amplitude, intervention, selected factor, or causal gate is opened.

opposing_outcomes.raw_additive_state_program: A-D pass. Raw Q does not prevent the sealed factorized H/R state program.
opposing_outcomes.raw_coupled_cell_program: A/B/D pass and C fails. H/R should target coupled cells rather than additive states.
opposing_outcomes.amplitude_is_document_continuous: A/D pass and B fails. Discrete normalized directions remain useful, but a raw H/R state program needs an input-derived amplitude variable or finer structure.
